author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The fix makes 'a page number below 1 is clamped to page 1' a guaranteed, tested behavior (OwnerControllerTests#processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage), but the Owner records Edge cases list (items 1-3) does not enumerate it. The list already documents comparably bounded cases (all-spaces search, missing-owner request) in the same style, and the PRD-authoring convention ties each numbered edge case to a dedicated test. Add a fourth edge case stating that an out-of-range page number is treated as the first page, so the new test has a citable edge-case number and future readers of the PRD know this behavior is guaranteed rather than incidental. This is a content addition, not autofix-eligible on the PRD path (edge-case items are excluded per document-writing/review-checks.md).

approved_aspects: The Math.max(page, 1) fix and its MockMvc test are correctly scoped to the OwnerController.processFindForm bug; the in-code comment above the clamp explains why (stale/hand-edited page links) rather than restating what the code does, meets the 30-word sentence guidance, and needs no ADR since it is a comment, not a durable design-doc claim
docs/system-design.md's Known Defects table has no stale entry for this bug (it was never listed there), so no removal is needed
Cross-document coherence holds: no requirement ID, constant, or config value in system-design.md or ubiquitous-language.md was invalidated by this change

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Class sweep for the finding class 'request-derived page index reaching PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) without a lower-bound clamp' found one further instance outside the change set: VetController.showVetList has the identical unclamped shape, so GET /vets.html?page=0 still reaches PageRequest.of(-1, 5) and surfaces the error page that security-principles records as rendering the underlying exception message. It is pre-existing and therefore not a defect of this change (per docs/security-principles.md, pre-existing baseline absences are never findings), but the codebase now carries two copies of the same boundary with opposite handling, which is the 'a demonstration teaches a reader something false' concern. Raising as a question for the requirement owner, not as a fix demand on this slice: is the vets pagination boundary in scope for a follow-up requirement?

approved_aspects: Lower-bound clamp sits at the trust boundary (controller entry) before the value is used, and the clamped local is threaded to both consumers (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) with no residual use of the raw parameter - matches the security-principles rule 'validate type, range, and shape before use'.
Math.max(page, 1) is overflow-safe at Integer.MIN_VALUE and strictly narrows the input domain; it adds no new trust boundary, sink, or attack surface.

No injection sink introduced: the value never composes query text (data access stays on the derived repository query findByLastNameStartingWith with a Pageable) and never composes a filesystem or resource path.

XSS/template-injection re-checked at the render sink: owners/ownersList.html splices currentPage into Thymeleaf preprocessing expressions (__${currentPage - 1}__ at lines 44 and 49), which is an expression-evaluation splice rather than an escaped output. It is safe here only because currentPage is a primitive int, so the spliced text can only be digits. The clamp additionally guarantees currentPage >= 1 at that sink.

Absent upper bound assessed independently and confirmed sound. An over-large page yields an empty Page, which the pre-existing isEmpty() branch handles by returning owners/findOwners, so addPaginationModel and its templates are never reached with currentPage > totalPages and no exception path opens. On resource exhaustion: Spring Data's AbstractPageRequest.getOffset() computes (long) pageNumber * (long) pageSize, so no int overflow is reachable even at page = Integer.MAX_VALUE, and the database cost of a large OFFSET is bounded by the table's row count, not by the offset value. No unbounded allocation is driven by the parameter, since pageSize is a fixed constant of 5 and is not request-derived. An upper clamp would be cosmetic, not a security control.
Change is a net reduction in exposure: it removes one reachable path into the error page that docs/security-principles.md records as rendering the underlying exception message outward.

Supply chain unchanged - the change set touches no build file (no build.gradle, no lockfile, no repository declaration) and adds no dependency, so the four dependency checks in system-design.md do not engage and no new CVE surface is introduced.
No secret material in the diff under any naming: the added identifiers are page, currentPage, pageBelowFirst, and pageable, all numeric or pagination state.
No mass-assignment change: the added parameter handling binds no new field and the Owner binder's identifier disallow list is untouched.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: New test method processFindFormWithPageBelowOneShowsFirstPage names the controller method under test, not the behavior. testing-principles.md § Test Naming mandates the BDD school (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward; this test is newly added in this change and falls squarely under that rule.
findings.fix: Rename to something like theOwnerSearchShouldClampPageBelowOneToTheFirstPage (or similar) so the name states the outcome a reader must verify, not the handler method invoked.

findings.description: The two boundary values (page=0, page=-1) are driven through a for-loop with inline MockMvc assertions inside the loop body. The test-review checklist (Test Structure) calls for straight-line test bodies and flags missing @ParameterizedTest for repetitive cases as an AUTOFIX issue; this is a new test written after the naming/structure rules took effect, so it should adopt the preferred idiom from the start rather than copy the pre-existing for-loop pattern used by an older sibling test (processFindFormIgnoresSurroundingWhitespace).
findings.fix: Convert to @ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource(ints = {0, -1}) (or @CsvSource) driving a single assertion block per invocation; keep the Pageable-capture assertion as a follow-up single-run test or aggregate it outside the parameterized cases.

approved_aspects: The test genuinely pins the fixed defect: it asserts both the user-visible currentPage model attribute (=1) and, via ArgumentCaptor, the actual zero-based Pageable.getPageNumber() (=0) sent to the repository for both page=0 and page=-1 — this would fail on the pre-fix code, where PageRequest.of(page-1, pageSize) receives a negative index and throws.

Boundary coverage is adequate for the defect's scope: 0 and -1 are the representative boundary and below-boundary values for a 1-based page parameter clamped at the handler entry; no PRD edge-case table entry exists for this parameter to check against.

Mocking stays within the brief's policy — MockMvc as the sanctioned HTTP-boundary stand-in, and Mockito stubbing/verification of the OwnerRepository collaborator (a persistence boundary), consistent with the rest of the existing suite.
./gradlew test passes for OwnerControllerTests including the new test.

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: Finding 1 (naming) resolved: theOwnerSearchShouldClampAPageBelowOneToTheFirstPage states the outcome under test per testing-principles.md's BDD school, no longer names the handler method.

Finding 2 (structure) resolved: the for-loop is replaced with @ParameterizedTest + @ValueSource(ints = {0, -1}) and a straight-line body, matching the Test Structure checklist's ban on loops in test bodies.

Keeping the ArgumentCaptor verify/assert inside each parameterized invocation is the stronger choice, not a regression: Spring's @MockitoBean reset fires per JUnit 5 TestTemplate invocation, so each of the two runs gets a fresh owners mock, verify(times(1))/requestedPage.getValue() checks that exact invocation's Pageable rather than pooling across runs. This is a tighter per-case assertion than the prior aggregated allSatisfy(pageable.getAllValues()) and needs no further split.
Test still pins the fixed defect: currentPage model attribute and the zero-based Pageable.getPageNumber() are both asserted for each boundary value (0, -1).
./gradlew test on OwnerControllerTests passes both parameterized invocations.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owners page parameter at the handler entry

blast_radius.note: Eight prod lines in one method of one controller plus its sibling test; two modules only because prod and test split, no sensitive paths, no build or config files, and the clamped local never escapes processFindForm.

semantic_surprise.note: Math.max(page, 1) is identity for every previously working page, so only the formerly-throwing page < 1 path changes; both consumers were rethreaded to currentPage with no residual use of the raw parameter, and the clamp is overflow-safe at Integer.MIN_VALUE where a page + 1 style fix would not be.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized test asserts real outcomes at both boundaries, the currentPage model attribute and the captured zero-based Pageable.getPageNumber(), so it fails against the pre-fix code where PageRequest.of(-1, 5) throws rather than merely restating the implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: Two of four approvals ride on unactioned clarify findings, the security-reviewer's naming a user-reachable identical defect in VetController, and the test-reviewer's round-one findings were both bar_clause tested-as-spec and only cleared after a rework round.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, consultations, and design revisions; the diff touches exactly the handler named in the requirement and its test, and the two out-of-scope observations were routed to product-requirements-expert rather than absorbed into this slice.

rationale: The code itself is as clean as a fix gets and needs no careful re-read. The attention is owed to the residual: GET /vets.html?page=0 still hits PageRequest.of(-1, 5), so the codebase now handles the identical boundary two opposite ways. Confirm the follow-up requirement and the PRD edge case are queued before merging.
